title: Delta, and why Theta Desk sells below 0.15
summary: Delta as price sensitivity and as a rough probability, and the trade-off behind the 0.15 rule.

questions.q: A call has delta 0.20. If the stock rises ₹10, the call's premium rises by about:
Roughly, a 0.12 delta option has what chance of expiring in the money?
questions.why: Delta, ignoring sign, approximates the probability of finishing ITM.

questions.q: Why does Theta Desk only sell strikes with |delta| < 0.15?
options: A normal month's move rarely reaches them
questions.why: Low-delta strikes are far enough away that typical moves don't reach them. They can still lose.

questions.q: Compared with a 0.30 delta strike, a 0.10 delta strike pays:
questions.why: Further away means less likely to pay out, so buyers pay less for it.

questions.q: Your short put's delta rose from 0.12 to 0.35. This means:
options: The stock moved towards your strike and risk has grown
questions.why: Rising delta on a short means the strike is getting closer and more likely to finish ITM.
